questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of a non­volatile memory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SDRAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Synchronous dynamic random-access memory (SDRAM)** is any DRAM where the **operation of its external pin interface** is coordinated by an **externally supplied clock signal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Non-volatile memory or non-volatile storage is a type of computer memory that can retain stored information even after power is removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **EEPROM **stands for **electrically erasable programmable read-only memory** and is a type of **non-volatile memory** used in computers.
 
• **Flash memory **is a type of **nonvolatile memory **that** erases data in units called blocks** and **rewrites **data at the byte level.
 
• **Hard disks are nonvolatile storage devices** that are used to store and retrieve data quickly.

questions.question: As per IMF’s January 2025 report, what is the projected global headline inflation rate for 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) January 2025 report, **the projected global headline inflation rate for 2025 is 4.2%.**
 
• Global headline inflation reflects the overall inflation rate across the world, considering both advanced and emerging economies.
 
• IMF projections are based on comprehensive economic models and data analysis from member countries.
 
• Factors contributing to the 2025 inflation projection include **monetary policies, geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, and energy market dynamics.**
 
• The IMF’s report serves as a critical reference for policymakers and economists to shape economic strategies globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Headline Inflation:**

 
 
• It measures the total inflation within an economy, including volatile elements such as food and energy prices.
 
• Unlike core inflation, headline inflation does not exclude specific categories like energy and food.
 
 
 
• **IMF and Inflation Projections:**
 
 
• The IMF publishes inflation forecasts in its World Economic Outlook reports, which are released several times a year.
 
• These forecasts are essential for global economic planning and policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Global Inflation:**
 
 
• Key factors include supply chain challenges, monetary policies, energy price fluctuations, and geopolitical instability.
 
• Central banks worldwide adjust interest rates to manage inflation levels effectively.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Inflation:**
 
 
• High inflation decreases purchasing power and increases the cost of living.
 
• Conversely, deflation (negative inflation) can lead to economic stagnation.

questions.question: According to the provision of which Article of the Constitution can the President of India ask for advice from the Supreme Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 143**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__**Article 143**__

__
 
• **As per Article 143**, **the President has the power to address questions to the Supreme Court, that he deems important for public welfare.**
 
• The Supreme Court “advises” the President by answering the query put before it.
 
• **Article 143** of the Constitution confers **Advisory Jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Article 143: Power of President to consult Supreme Court.**

 
• **If at any time it appears to the President that a question of law or fact has arisen**, or is likely to arise, which is of such a nature and such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Supreme Court upon it, he may refer the question to that Court for consideration and the Court may, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon.
 
• **The President may, notwithstanding anything in the proviso to article 131,** refer a dispute of the kind mentioned in the said proviso to the Supreme Court for opinion and the Supreme Court shall, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon.

questions.question: The term ‘Dribble’ is generally associated with______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term '**dribble**' is used in **Basketball**.
 
• In basketball, dribbling is **bouncing the ball on the floor continuously with one hand at a time**.
 
• It is the **only legal way that a player may maintain possession of the ball **while walking or running.
 
• The dribble allows for much faster advancement and thus more opportunities for scoring.
 
• It also provides an opportunity for a crafty player on the opposing team to "steal" the ball in mid-bounce.
 
• **Dribbling should be done with finger pads and the fingers **should be relaxed and spread.
 
• The wrist should be pushing the basketball, and the forearm should be moving up and down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basketball is a team sport in which there are two teams of five players each**.
 
• Players advance the ball by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling) or by passing it to a teammate.
 
• On offense, players may use a variety of shots – **the layup, the jump shot, or a dunk; on defense.**
 
• They may steal the ball from a **dribbler, intercept passes, or block shots; either offense or defense may collect a rebound.**
 
• It is a violation to lift or drag one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands and then resume dribbling.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holding property**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holding property** is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India.
 
• Conditions for acquiring Indian citizenship include **domicile, descent, and registration**.
 
• Citizenship can also be acquired by **naturalization** under specific conditions.
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** outlines the various modes and conditions for acquiring Indian citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** provides for acquisition and termination of citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• The Act also provides for the renunciation and termination of citizenship.
 
• Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) are provided certain benefits but are not considered Indian citizens.
 
• Recent amendments, such as the **Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019**, have also impacted the criteria and process for acquiring Indian citizenship.

questions.question: The words like chishti, suhrawardi and pyadasi are related to which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sufi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sufi** is a mystical Islamic belief and practice in which Muslims seek to find the truth of divine love and knowledge through direct personal experience of God.
 
• The terms **Chishti** and **Suhrawardi** refer to two major Sufi orders or Silsilas in Islam.
 
• The **Chishti Order** was founded in Chisht, a small town near Herat, Afghanistan, and is known for its emphasis on love, tolerance, and openness.
 
• The **Suhrawardi Order** was founded by Abu Najib as-Suhrawardi and later popularized by his nephew, Shihab ad-Din Abu Hafs Umar Suhrawardi. This order emphasizes strict adherence to Islamic law and the importance of spiritual guidance from a Sufi master.
 
• These Sufi orders played a significant role in the spread of Islam in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nathpati**__

 __
 
• The **Nathpati** tradition is a Hindu religious movement that originated in India.
 
• It is a form of Shaivism that emphasizes the worship of Shiva.
 
• The Nath sect is known for its ascetic practices and has a significant influence on Indian culture and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Islam**__
 __
 
• **Islam** is a monotheistic Abrahamic religion founded on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad.
 
• It is the second-largest religion in the world with over 1.9 billion followers.
 
• The primary religious texts of Islam are the Quran and Hadith.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnav**__
 
 
• **Vaishnavism** is a tradition within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, such as Krishna and Rama.
 
• It is one of the major traditions of Hinduism, alongside Shaivism, Shaktism, and Smartism.
 
• Vaishnavism emphasizes devotion (bhakti) to Vishnu and his incarnations.

questions.question: In the context of Sufi traditions, what is the meaning of the word 'sama'?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **In the context of Sufi traditions, the meaning of the word 'sama' is the Recitation of holy songs**__.
 
• **Sama** is a Sufi ceremony performed as dhikr. Sama means "listening", while dhikr means "remembrance".
 __
 
• These performances often include singing, playing instruments, dancing, recitation of poetry and prayers, wearing symbolic attire, and other rituals.
 
• Sama is a particularly popular form of **worship in Sufism**.
 
• In 2008, UNESCO confirmed the "Mevlevi Sama Ceremony" of Turkey as one of the Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sufism**, also known as Tasawwuf, is a mystic body of religious practice within Islam characterized by a focus on Islamic spirituality, ritualism, asceticism, and esotericism.

questions.question: 'Memoirs of Babur' or 'Baburnama', also known as 'Tuzk-e Babri', was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Babur.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur has written his biography i.e. Baburnama which is also known as Tuzk-e Babri. Babur and Jahangir are the only two emperors of the Mughal Empire who wrote their own biographies.**
 
• Baburnama is also known to be the first true autobiography in Islamic literature.
 
• Baburnama was written in **Chagatai Turkic**, which was Babur's mother tongue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuzk-e Babri** is written in the Chagatai language, known to Babur as Turki (meaning Turkic), the spoken language of the Timurids.
 
• As the Mughals were Chaghtai Turks by origin, Turkish was their mother tongue.
 
• Tuzk-e Babri is the memoirs of **Zahir-ud-Dīn Muhammad Bābur (1483- 1530),** founder of the Mughal Empire and a great-great-great-grandson of Timur.
 
• During Emperor Akbar's reign, the work was completely translated to Persian, the usual literary language of the Mughal court by a Mughal

 courtier, Abdul Rahim.
 
• It was Akbar who consciously set out to make Persian the leading language of the Mughal court.

questions.question: Which of the following network devices is used for connecting larger LAN network with the smaller LAN networks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bridge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Networking devices** are physical devices that allow computer networks to establish communication with each other. 

 
 
• Different network devices are **Modems, Bridges, Switches, Gateway **etc.
 
 
 
• **A Bridge is a device in the computer used to connect larger LANs with a group of smaller LANs. Hence option 3 is correct.**
 
 
• It operates in the Data Link layer in the OSI model.
 
 
 
• **Bridges use Media Access Control (MAC) address to transfer data packets (also called frames) and bridge uses the MAC address to forward the data or blocks it. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Gateway acts as a connection between different dissimilar networks or it interprets and transfers the data from one network protocol to another**.

 
 
• Gateways are also called protocol converters.
 
 
 
• **A Modem is a networking device that modulates digital data from a computer into analog signals for transmission.**
 
• **A Switch is a multiport device that connects devices within the network and transmits the data packets between the devices**.
 
 
• They read the hardware addresses of the incoming data packets and forward them to the correct destination.

questions.question: At high doses, ______ kills cancer cells or slows their growth by damaging their DNA. Cancer cells whose DNA is damaged beyond repair stop dividing or die. When the damaged cells die, they are broken down and removed by the body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiation therapy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Radiotherapy to treat cancer:

 
 
• High doses of radiation are used in radiation therapy, also known as radiotherapy, as a cancer treatment to eradicate cancer cells and reduce tumour size.
 
• As with X-rays of your teeth or shattered bones, radiation is utilised at low doses in x-rays to see inside your body.
 
• Radiation therapy damages cancer cells' DNA, which either kills them or limits their growth at high dosages.
 
• Cancer cells that have DNA damage that cannot be repaired either cease proliferating or die.
 
• When the injured cells expire, the body degrades and eliminates them.
 
• But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA.
 
• This can cause serious health problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemotherapy **

 
 
• Chemotherapy is the use of any drug to treat any disease.
 
• But to most people, the word chemotherapy means drugs used for** cancer treatment**. 
 
• It's often shortened to “chemo.” Surgery and radiation therapy remove, kill, or damage cancer cells in a certain area, but chemo can work throughout the whole body.
 
 

 
• Surgery:

 
 
• Surgery is a medical speciality that employs operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to examine or treat a pathological condition.
 
• Such as a disease or injury, to enhance bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwelcome ruptured areas
 
 
 
• **Physiotherapy**
 
 
• ​Physiotherapy is a healthcare profession that aims to help people restore and maintain movement and function when affected by** injury**, **illness** or **disability**.
 
• Physiotherapists use a combination of manual **therapy**, **exercise**, and **education**.

questions.question: During the reign of Kanishka, Buddhism for the first time went to China and from China, it went to
questions.solution:
During the reign of Kanishka, Buddhism for the first time went to China and from China, it went to __**Korea and Japan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Kanishka was the greatest ruler of the Kushan Empire, which ruled over much of Central Asia and northwest India from the 1st to the 3rd centuries CE. 
 
• He was a great patron of Buddhism and is credited with spreading the religion to China.
 
• The first documented **introduction of Buddhism to China was in the 2nd century CE,** during the reign of Kanishka's successor,** Huvishka. **
 
• This was likely due to the travels of Buddhist monks along the **Silk Road**, which connected China with Central Asia and India.
 
• From China, Buddhism spread to Korea and Japan in the following centuries. 
 
• It became one of the major religions in these countries and played an important role in their cultures.
 
• Here are some of the key events in the spread of Buddhism from India to China:
 
 
• ​**1st century CE**: Buddhism first arrived in China along the Silk Road.
 
• **2nd century CE**: The Kushan Empire sponsors the translation of Buddhist texts into Chinese.
 
• **3rd century CE**: Buddhism becomes established in China.
 
• **4th century CE**: Buddhism began to spread to Korea.
 
• **6th century CE**: Buddhism began to spread to Japan.
 
 
 
• Buddhism has had a profound impact on the cultures of China, Korea, and Japan. 
 
• It has influenced their** art, literature, and philosophy. **
 
• It has also helped to shape their values and worldviews.

questions.question: Majority of the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by:

options.text: the political parties that oppose the majority party
the elected members or ministers of different areas
the elected members of the legislative Assemblies of various states.

questions.solution:
Majority of the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by __**the elected members of the legislative Assemblies of various states.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament, and it is **composed of 250 members. **
 
• Of these members, **238 are elected **by the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the various states. 
 
• The remaining** 12 members are nominated by the President of India.**
 
• The method of election for the Rajya Sabha is proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. 
 
• This means that each voter has a number of votes equal to the number of seats that are being contested in their state. 
 
• They can cast their votes for as many candidates as they like, but they cannot give more than one vote to any one candidate.
 
• The votes are then counted, and the candidates who receive the most votes are elected. 
 
• If no candidate receives the majority of the votes, then the votes are transferred to the other candidates according to the preferences of the voters. 
 
• This process continues until all of the seats have been filled. 
 
• The **Rajya Sabha is a very important part **of the Indian Parliament. 
 
• It has the power to pass laws, approve the appointment of the Prime Minister, and impeach the President. 
 
• It also has the power to review laws passed by the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament. 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is designed to represent the interests of the states in the Indian Parliament. 
 
• The fact that the majority of its members are elected by the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the various states ensures that the states have a strong voice in the national decision-making process.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to acquire citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Renunciation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Renunciation** is not a way to acquire citizenship in India; rather, it is a way to voluntarily give up Indian citizenship.
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides various modes for acquiring Indian citizenship, including **by birth, descent, registration, and naturalization**.
 
• **Incorporation of territory** is another mode where a new territory becomes a part of India, and the government may specify the persons who shall be citizens of India.
 
• Citizenship by **registration** is available to certain categories of persons such as persons of Indian origin who are ordinarily resident in India and other specified categories.
 
• Citizenship by **birth** is applicable to individuals born in India on or after January 26, 1950, but before July 1, 1987, and to individuals born on or after July 1, 1987, if either parent is a citizen of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, also provides for the termination and deprivation of citizenship under specific conditions.
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act and can be done by any citizen of India who is also a citizen or national of another country.
 
• Upon renunciation, the individual ceases to be a citizen of India, and any minor child of that person also loses Indian citizenship.
 
• The process of renunciation is outlined in the Citizenship Rules, and it requires the individual to make a declaration in the prescribed manner.
 
• It's important for individuals to be aware of the implications of renunciation, including the loss of rights and privileges associated with Indian citizenship.

questions.question: Kathak dance is known as combination of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Music, dance and narrative**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It is known for its intricate **footwork, spins, and expressive gestures**.
 
• Kathak incorporates **music, dance, and narrative** elements to convey stories, often from ancient Indian epics and mythology.
 
• The narrative aspect of Kathak is delivered through **mime and facial expressions**, making it a unique blend of various artistic components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The name **Kathak** is derived from the Sanskrit word **'Katha'** meaning story, and **'Kathakar'** meaning storyteller.
 
• Historically, Kathak dancers, known as **Kathakars**, used to travel and narrate stories through dance and music.
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Bhakti movement** and later under the patronage of Mughal rulers, which added Persian influences to its style.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, and it continues to be a popular performance art both in India and globally.

questions.question: The second five-year plan introduced to the concept of public sector of state-run enterprises based on the ____________ model of industrialisation.

• PC Mahalanobis established the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta in 1931 and for the same reason, he is known as the father of Indian Statistics. He was a member of the first Planning Commission of free India.
 
• The second five-year plan was for the year 1956-1961, this plan was based on the **Russian** model of industrialization.
 
• The second five-year plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid Industrialisation. The plan attempted to determine a balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors in order to maximize long-run economic growth. 
 
• As a result, hydroelectric power projects across the country and five steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of Russia, Britain (the U.K), and West Germany respectively. Coal production was increased. More railway lines were added all over the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **E-Hansa Development:** The E-Hansa is being developed by CSIR-NAL, Bengaluru, and is a two-seater electric trainer aircraft designed for affordable pilot training.
 
• **Cost-Effective:** With a cost of around ₹2 crore, it is about half the price of imported trainer aircraft, making it a viable option for flying clubs and aviation academies.
 
• **Green Aviation:** The E-Hansa supports India's green aviation goals by using electric propulsion powered by clean energy, reducing carbon emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HANSA-3 Program:** The E-Hansa is part of the HANSA-3 program, aimed at enhancing India’s aerospace self-reliance and boosting pilot training capabilities.
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships:** The government is promoting public-private partnerships to commercialize the E-Hansa and encourage private sector involvement in aerospace research and development.

 [IMAGE: https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf38xF_pn74km_sseRvL7FujgSldkFpCbbZyF98aBiplLPWi4Hr5XC_i7DHsjaJ1MyPHt-YUkxV8jMZdkzytAR_29ocYgQAgIuoinLt0deq1FP1KVDfcq_69KjjFOU7Xet8teZp?key=Iy0AqN3zEWvZI2fJLuOSCg]

questions.question: Baba Farid was associated with which of the following region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Punjab__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was succeeded in Delhi by his khalifa, Khwaja Fariduddin Masud (1175-1265) known as Ganjshakar and more popularly as Baba Farid.**
 
• **Baba Farid left Delhi for Ajodhan in Punjab and lived in his khanqah there. Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.**
 
• He despised association with the ruling class and rich persons.
 
• **Nathpanthi yogis** also visited his khanqah and discussed with him the nature of mysticism.
 
• His popularity in Punjab is clear from the fact that more than three hundred years after his death, verses ascribed to him were included in** the Adi Granth compiled by the fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan, in 1604.**
 
• His tomb at **Pakpatan** soon developed into a center of pilgrimage. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​The most celebrated disciple of Baba Farid and the greatest sufi saint of the 14th century was Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya (1236-1325).**
 
• He made **Delhi the most famous center of the Chishti order.**
 
• Two historians **Ziauddin Barani and Amir Khusrau**, who were his contemporaries, testify to his eminent position in the social and religious life of Northern India during the late 13th and early 14th centuries.
 
• Later, his successors spread the Chishti order in various parts of the country.
 
• His teachings and **conversations (malfuzat) are recorded in Fawaid-ul Fuwad written by Amir Hasan Sijzi.**
 
• This work serves more as a guide to practical aspects of Sufism than as a treatise on its metaphysical and theosophical aspects.
